resources.string: All your hosts in good hands
Where does HostMan run? You can change this later in the app\'s settings.
HostMan runs on another machine — usually a Raspberry Pi on your network — and this phone opens it, like a browser would.
Server address, e.g. nakedpi.local or 192.168.2.123 (port 8899 unless you say)
No HostMan answered. Type its address instead — an older HostMan does not answer the search.

The whole of HostMan runs here, with its own SSH key and database: add hosts, deploy apps, open shells, all from the phone. It cannot manage the phone itself, and nothing runs while the phone is off the network.
This build of the app, or this phone\'s processor, has no HostMan server in it. Connect to a server instead.
HostMan on this phone would not start.
HostMan on this phone did not accept the app\'s PIN.
%1$s has a certificate this phone does not trust. Install its CA in Android\'s settings, or connect over http on your own network.
No app on this phone opens that link.
HostMan is running on this phone
Only this phone can reach it.
Open http://%1$s:%2$d on another device on this network.
Full stack: HostMan, its SSH key and its database are all on this phone. Turn off to open a HostMan that runs on another machine.
Thin client: HostMan runs on another machine and this phone opens it. Turn on to run the whole of HostMan here.
Lists the HostMan servers that answer on this Wi-Fi.
Serve other devices on this network
Only this phone can open HostMan.
Laptops and other phones on this network can open it, with the PIN. The connection is not encrypted.
Choose a PIN of at least four characters first: other devices sign in with it, because this HostMan can run commands as root on every host.
Set. Other devices sign in with it; this app signs itself in.
None. Only this app can sign in, with a secret of its own.
Keep running when the app is closed
Health checks and port forwards carry on, and other devices can still reach it. Shows a notification while it runs.
What a network search lists this phone\'s HostMan as: %1$s
What HostMan on this phone has said lately.
In this app\'s private storage, with its SSH key. Uninstalling the app deletes both: the hosts you set up will need the new key that a reinstall makes.
A deployment you start or open keeps a notification with its latest output, and says how it ended, after you leave the app.
Not running: exited with status %1$d. See the server log.
